menu_options.modbus: Modbus in Home Assistant (e.g. Elfin EW11)

esphome.title: Marstek Goedkoop Laden
esphome.description: Pick the price sensor and the Marstek entities (LilyGO RS485). Recognised entities are filled in already.

data_description.price_entity: Sensor that holds the published hourly prices in an attribute, for example the Zonneplan hourly tariff sensor.
data_description.control_mode_entity: Master switch for forcing: enable or disable.
data_description.force_mode_entity: Direction when forcing: charge, discharge or stop.
data_description.force_power_entity: Set to the spread-out power while charging.
data_description.max_power_entity: Sets the number of charge hours and the upper limit of the power. Empty = 2500 W.
data_description.capacity_entity: Empty = the fixed capacity from the options.
data_description.charged_energy_entity: Together with the discharged energy this sets the efficiency. Empty = fixed efficiency.
data_description.force_discharge_power_entity: Needed for selling. Empty = selling is not possible.
data_description.max_discharge_power_entity: Upper limit of the sell power. Empty = 2500 W.
data_description.min_soc_entity: The Marstek does not discharge below this SoC. Empty = the fixed value from the options.

modbus.title: Marstek Goedkoop Laden
modbus.description: Pick the price sensor and the Modbus register sensors of the Marstek (for example from MarstekVenus-ElfinEW11 or, for a Venus E v3 over Ethernet, MarstekVenusV3-modbus-TCP-IP). Writing goes through the Modbus hub you name here. Maximum power and capacity are optional; with the maximum discharge power, Hold and No loss work too.

data_description.price_entity: Sensor that holds the published hourly prices in an attribute, for example the Zonneplan hourly tariff sensor.
data_description.modbus_hub: The name of the hub in your modbus: configuration, for example MarstekVenus.

marstek_modbus.title: Marstek Goedkoop Laden
marstek_modbus.description: Pick the price sensor and the entities of the Marstek Venus Modbus integration (ViperRNMC), which can talk to a Venus E v3 directly over Ethernet. In that integration, enable the RS485 control mode switch and the force mode select first: they are disabled by default.

init.title: Options
init.description: Change the entities or the planning rule. The integration reloads afterwards.

data_description.language: Language of the plan text, flow chart and cards. Automatic follows the Home Assistant language.

data.default_efficiency: Efficiency when the counters are missing

data_description.default_efficiency: The efficiency is calculated from the Marstek energy counters (total discharged divided by total charged). This fixed value only applies when those counters are not set or have no value.
data_description.battery_price: Purchase price of the battery in euros, for depreciation. 0 means no depreciation is counted.
data_description.battery_cycles: Number of full cycles the battery is expected to last. Depreciation per kWh = price ÷ (cycles × capacity).
data_description.min_soc: Only used when no discharge cut-off entity is set.

data.top_hours: Number of most expensive hours to compare with

data_description.margin: After the charging loss, charging has to gain at least this amount.
data_description.top_hours: An hour is cheap enough when its price is below the efficiency times the average of these most expensive hours after it, minus the margin.
data_description.min_lookahead_hours: Hours with fewer known prices after them are ignored.

data.negative_strategy: Negative price: how to divide the energy

data_description.negative_price_limit: Below this hourly price the battery always charges at full power (when the switch is on). Default 0: only at a truly negative price.
data_description.negative_strategy: Spread by value: more in the more negative hours, lower power. Maximum gain: fill the best hours first at full power.

data.solar_learn: Learn the reliability from the actual production

data_description.use_solar_forecast: Takes the expected solar yield from the Energy dashboard into account when charging at night, so there is room for the sun.
data_description.solar_learn: Compares each day's solar forecast with what the panels really produced (from the Energy dashboard) and uses the median of the last days as the reliability once there are at least 3 days. Until then the reliability below is used.
data_description.solar_reliability: The part of the forecast to count on. Lower is more careful.
data_description.house_power_entity: Optional. A power sensor (W or kW) with the total power the house uses, without the battery. The integration learns your average consumption per hour of the day (weekdays and weekends separately) and uses it for the solar surplus instead of the fixed own consumption.

data_description.sell_margin: Selling only happens when the sell price exceeds the cost of recharging (charge price divided by the efficiency) plus this amount.
data_description.house_power: Sets the reserve: this power times the hours until recharging stays in the battery.
data_description.sell_price_factor: Sell price = hourly price times this factor, minus the deduction. With net metering: 1 and 0. Without, for example 0.826 and 0.108 for the bare market price.
